articles.title: Dollar Rebounds and Central Bank Decisions Loom Ahead of Key Data
articles.intro: The US dollar hits a two-week high and rebounds as the euro slips on French worries and key central bank decisions approach. Meanwhile, sterling steadies and gilts tick up following Healey’s UK Budget.

sections.p: Market sentiment remains cautious as traders prepare for a heavy schedule of central bank rate decisions and tier-one economic data. The dollar index has found renewed strength, hitting a two-week high while Treasury yields nudge toward one-week highs. European currencies face pressure, with the euro slipping on French worries and the Polish zloty falling to its weakest level since November 2023. Sterling has steadied and gilts ticked up following Healey’s UK Budget, which unveiled a bank tax and energy bill support alongside unchanged tax thresholds.

Attention is heavily focused on upcoming macroeconomic releases and monetary policy events. The Canadian dollar has held gains and steadied after a seven-day rally following a Bank of Canada rate hike, though it recently slipped as investors await further central bank clarity. Across the board, market participants are weighing the implications of upcoming US Advance GDP and Core PCE Price Index figures alongside looming Federal Reserve, ECB, and BOJ policy meetings.

In currency markets, EUR/USD trades in a downtrend at 1.1133 with an RSI of 40.4, bounded by support at 1.1133 and resistance at 1.1298. GBP/USD holds a sideways trend at 1.32876 with an RSI of 61.3, looking toward support at 1.32008 and resistance at 1.34018. USD/CAD sits sideways at 1.4047 with an oversold RSI of 23.2, with support at 1.3995 and resistance at 1.4262. Commitment of Traders data shows net short positioning persisting in major currencies like EUR, GBP, and AUD, while USD Index net longs stand at 15,044 contracts with 65.1% of open interest on the long side.

Traders should closely monitor the upcoming US Advance GDP q/q and Core PCE Price Index m/m releases scheduled for October 29, 2026. Additionally, the ECB Main Refinancing Rate and Monetary Policy Statement on October 29, followed by the BOJ Policy Rate and Outlook Report on October 30, will provide vital volatility catalysts for global FX pairs.

articles.title: Dollar Hits Two-Week High Ahead of Fed Decision and Central Bank Deluge
articles.intro: The US dollar climbed to a two-week high as global investors braced for a crucial Federal Reserve rate decision alongside key announcements from other major central banks. Meanwhile, sterling dipped while European currencies felt the weight of localized political concerns.

sections.p: The broader market sentiment remains cautious and heavily defensive as participants prepare for high-impact monetary policy updates. The dollar rebounds firmly as the euro slips on French worries, while the Canadian dollar steadies after a seven-day rally ahead of rate decisions. U.S. Treasury yields hover near multi-week lows, keeping traders alert to potential volatility spikes across major currency pairs.

The dominant catalyst for forex flows is the impending Federal Reserve decision, with the Federal Funds Rate forecast to hold at 4.00%. Concurrently, currency markets are digesting the upcoming Bank of Canada rate decision alongside the annual UK budget release and looming central bank announcements. Regional pressures, such as AI jitters supporting the Japanese yen and regional political worries dragging on European units, continue to shape cross-asset movements.

Looking at the technical landscape, EUR/USD trades in a downtrend at 1.115 with an RSI of 44.9, sitting right at support with resistance eyed at 1.3355 for broader context. GBP/USD trades sideways around 1.3328 with an RSI of 69.2, while USD/CAD rests at 1.4023 showing an oversold RSI of 20.2. Commitment of Traders data shows net positioning remains heavily short on EUR at -134,524 and GBP at -80,420, contrasted by net long positioning on the USD Index at 15,044 and Gold at 199,865.

Traders should closely monitor the upcoming calendar events, featuring the Federal Funds Rate announcement and the Bank of Canada overnight rate decision expected at 2.50%. Additional attention will go toward the UK Annual Budget Release and ongoing developments in US yields as market participants position for potential policy surprises.

articles.title: Forex Daily Market Brief: Dollar Holds Firm and Yields Hover Ahead of Central Bank Decisions
articles.intro: Asian currencies mixed as the dollar holds firm and the yen retreats ahead of upcoming Federal Reserve decisions. Meanwhile, Treasury yields hover near three-week lows as AI jitters spur safe-haven demand.

sections.p: The broader market mood is characterized by cautious consolidation as participants weigh shifting fundamental pressures. Asian currencies remain mixed while the dollar rebounds and the euro slips ahead of key central bank decisions. At the same time, artificial intelligence jitters have spurred notable safe-haven bids, weighing on risk sentiment and driving Treasury yields toward their third consecutive weekly drop.

Macroeconomic attention is heavily focused on upcoming monetary policy events, including the Federal Reserve decision, Bank of Canada rate decisions, and the RBNZ Official Cash Rate statement projected alongside the Annual Budget Release for the UK. Market participants are closely monitoring these central bank trajectories while digesting secondary developments, such as Brazil's real weakening 12% following Lula's election victory and ongoing corporate technology headlines.

On the technical front, EUR/USD continues in a defined downtrend trading at 1.11881 with an RSI of 37.4, holding near support at 1.11771 and resistance at 1.1355. GBP/USD moves sideways at 1.33476 with an RSI of 59.6, bounded by support at 1.32008 and resistance at 1.34018. USD/CAD prints sideways at 1.4028 with an oversold RSI of 21.1, sitting between support at 1.3995 and resistance at 1.4262. Commitment of Traders data shows net positioning remaining heavily short on EUR at -134,524 contracts and GBP at -80,420 contracts, while USD Index net longs stand at 15,044 contracts.

Traders should look ahead to a busy economic calendar featuring upcoming Australian CPI data, New Zealand's Official Cash Rate announcements, and the critical central bank rate decisions from Canada and the United States. Keeping a close eye on these high-impact releases will be vital for assessing near-term volatility and liquidity shifts.
